Welcome

This is a secret worship tunnel with the Lord.

Birth is precious. It is not only a medical event or something to get through; it can be an intimate place where you meet God in a way that belongs to you. This course will give you practical preparation, but it will never ask you to earn a certain outcome. You are here to prepare with expectation, wisdom, and peace.

Move through the course in order the first time. Later, return to the module you need. Your job is not to master every word. Let the truth become familiar: God is present, your body has wisdom, your preparation matters, and favor is a gift.

My birth stories

Five natural births. Five settings. One faithful God.

I am a plus-size mom of six with five natural births. I share these stories to give you hope, not a standard to recreate. Every birth was different; the thread that grew stronger in me was a trust that God could meet me in my real body, real circumstances, and real unknowns.

Birth one: hospital water birth

My first natural birth was in a hospital water birth and about ninety percent pain-free. It showed me that a hospital room could still make space for movement, water, worship, and peace.

Birth two: hospital, pain-free

My second hospital birth was completely pain-free. It grew my expectation that birth did not have to mirror the fearful story I had been handed.

Birth three: birthing inn

My third at a birthing inn was the first I call truly supernatural and pain-free. God became even more personal in the birth space.

Birth four: planned home birth

My fourth was planned at home and pain-free except for one moment. I learned that intensity or a hard moment does not erase peace.

Birth five: unexpected home birth

My fifth became an unplanned husband-and-wife birth before the midwives arrived—peaceful and about an hour and a half. It taught me to keep the space simple and stay with the next wave.

My stories are testimonies, not formulas. I am inviting you to carry the principles—peace, preparation, worship, wise support, listening to the Holy Spirit—into the story God writes with you.

Module one • favor + your fastest secret

“I am not going into labor. I am going into favor.”

This is the posture: not by your striving, perfect plan, pain tolerance, or ability to control the room. “It is not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit,” says the Lord (Zechariah 4:6). “It is by grace... not by works” (Ephesians 2:8–9). Ask God for favor over your body, baby, timing, support people, and every decision that comes.

My fastest-birth secret is giving thanks through every contraction. A wave becomes an offering: “Thank You, God, You are here. Thank You, my body can open. Thank You, this wave is bringing my baby closer.” Then rest when it ends. Thanksgiving does not make you perform; it turns your attention away from fearful spiraling and toward God’s presence.

Why this supports the body too

Oxytocin is central to labor contractions and is supported by connection, warmth, privacy, and feeling safe. Giving thanks is one of the ways I intentionally help my brain move toward oxytocin and connection in labor. Gratitude shifts attention from fear to God’s presence, and that calmer, connected state supports the oxytocin system. Other natural oxytocin supports are affectionate touch, kissing, eye contact, a husband’s reassurance, privacy, dim lights, warm water, laughter, nipple stimulation, feeling unobserved, worship, slow breathing, and a room where Mom feels safe.

Beginning of the wave

“Thank You, God, You are with me.” Breathe down into the ribs and belly.

Middle of the wave

“Thank You, my body can open.” Keep the jaw loose and make sound if it helps.

End of the wave

“Thank You, that wave is complete.” Let the whole body melt between waves.

Partner’s part: give thanks too

Do not only coach her - worship with her. Say: “Thank You, God, for her strength. Thank You for this baby. Thank You that her body knows what to do. Thank You for every wave bringing our baby closer.” Keep your voice low, warm, and full of faith: “You are safe. One wave at a time. God is here.”

Dream with God

Co-partner with the Holy Spirit over the birth you desire.

You are allowed to have holy hopes. This is not about trying to control every detail or treating a dream as a contract with God. It is about bringing your desire out into the light, asking what peace looks like, and preparing an atmosphere where you can receive His instruction.

Make a little “dream with God” date. Grab your favorite pen, a warm drink, and ten quiet minutes. Start with: “Holy Spirit, what do You want me to know about this birth? What kind of atmosphere are You inviting me to prepare?” Write without editing.

What do I want to feel?

Finish: “In my birth space, I want to feel…” Think privacy, courage, warmth, worship, connection, safety, laughter, or quiet.

What do I want to hear?

Write three phrases for your husband or support person: “You are safe.” “One wave at a time.” “You are doing this with God.”

What do I want to see?

Picture lights, music, water, food, people, smells, and words. What belongs? What needs to be guarded?

What am I releasing?

Name one fear, borrowed story, or pressure. Ask Jesus what truth He wants to give you instead.

Dream-birth prayer

“Holy Spirit, I welcome You into my hopes and my unknowns. Show me what peace looks like for this birth. Help me prepare with wisdom and release control. I receive Your favor, Your presence, and the story You are writing with me.”

Module two • physiological childbirth

God designed your body to respond, open, and bring forth.

Physiological birth is the coordinated conversation between brain, hormones, uterus, cervix, baby, breath, posture, and environment. Your body is not a machine that must be forced into labor. In a typical unfolding, the upper uterus works in powerful waves while the lower uterine segment and cervix soften and yield; baby flexes, rotates, and descends.

Early labor: safety and oxytocin

Oxytocin helps coordinate contractions. Privacy, low lights, affectionate connection, feeling unobserved, water, warmth, and familiar voices can support the safety cues that let a mother turn inward. Early labor is often a time to rest, eat, hydrate, and not rush to perform labor.

Active labor: endorphins and focus

Endorphins are the body’s own coping hormones. They can support inward focus as waves intensify. Melatonin works alongside oxytocin, which helps explain why quiet and dimness can feel so good. A low moan, slow exhale, forward lean, or worship song can be practical tools.

Transition: adrenaline has a purpose

Adrenaline is protective, not bad. Too much early stress can make it harder to soften; later in labor, an adrenaline surge can bring energy for the final stretch. When doubt gets loud, lower stimulation and return to one wave—not the whole story.

Pushing: follow the body

Many women feel a strong urge and benefit from changing positions. Upright, side-lying, kneeling, forward-leaning, and supported squat positions can give the sacrum and tailbone room to respond. You do not have to be frozen in one posture.

The physiological pushing phase: trust the lead from within.

Pushing is not meant to become a performance. As baby moves low, many women describe a powerful, involuntary urge—sometimes called the fetal ejection reflex. It is the body’s own coordinated signal that baby is descending and the uterus is doing its work. You do not have to manufacture that moment with fear or force. Trust your body. Trust Holy Spirit to lead you. There are practical tools, but ultimately Holy Spirit is your source. He knows how to bring back the right posture, the right breath, the right thought, and the right word in the moment you need it.

That was my experience. Holy Spirit gave me a dream of being in a high lunge. When I was about to birth, He brought that dream back to me, and it was exactly what I needed. Do not dismiss a posture simply because it is not the one you expected. Birth is movement. If you feel led to get up, lean, kneel, sway, get into the water, shift your legs, or take a different angle, pay attention. You are not trying to look like anyone else’s birth. You are partnering with the body God gave you and the instruction He brings you.

High lunge

One foot forward, one foot back, hands supported on the bed, wall, partner, or chair. This can create an asymmetrical opening and was the position Holy Spirit showed me in a dream.

Forward-leaning kneel

Kneel over the bed, birth ball, or a stack of pillows. Let your belly hang, relax your jaw, and keep your back body wide.

Hands-and-knees

Use the bed, floor, or a mat. This makes room for movement and can help you stay instinctive and inward.

Supported squat

Hold a partner, bar, doorway, or sheet. Let your heels be supported if needed and keep the squat responsive—not forced or held for a performance.

Side-lying

Rest on your side with your upper leg supported. This can be a softer, restful posture while still giving your pelvis room.

Standing + leaning

Lean into your husband, the bed, or a counter. Sway, bend your knees, and let your body choose the rhythm.

Open mouth, open throat, open body.

One of the simplest reminders is: keep your mouth soft. Relax your tongue, lips, jaw, shoulders, and hands. Many women find a long low moo helps them stay open instead of clenching. You can make a low “mooooo” sound down into your belly on the exhale, not a tight high scream up in the throat. If your body asks for smaller, gentler breaths as baby’s head is close, try soft panting: little open-mouth exhales—“huh, huh, huh”—while staying relaxed. The purpose is not to follow a rule; it is to help you stay connected, soften, and listen.

Do not give the “ring of fire” a throne in your mind.

You may hear that phrase repeated so often that your mind begins preparing to create the experience before you ever get there. I do not want you rehearsing it. Sensations at crowning vary, and you do not have to build an expectation of suffering around someone else’s words. When your mind wants to race ahead, come back to: “This is one moment. God is with me. My body knows what to do. I can soften and follow the next instruction.” If your body signals slow down, soften, pant, change position, or pause, receive that as information—not panic.

Turn crowning into a weapon of glory.

Scripture repeatedly uses a crown as a picture of honor, beauty, victory, and God’s own covering: “You shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord” (Isaiah 62:3); “a crown of glory” (Isaiah 28:5); “the crown of life” (James 1:12). When baby is crowning, do not let fear name the moment. Let heaven name it. This is not a threat; it is a crown of glory. It is the visible sign that you are meeting your baby. Speak: “Father, I receive this crowning as a crown of beauty in Your hand. I will not partner with fear. I receive Your glory, Your strength, Your covering, and Your next instruction. My body is opening. My baby is coming. I am safe in Your presence.”

My nervous-system practice: ice, thanksgiving, Scripture, breath.

During pregnancy, I would hold ice and practice staying soft. I would give thanks, quote Scripture, and breathe instead of clenching. This gave my nervous system a small rehearsal: sensation does not have to equal panic. Try it simply. Hold an ice cube in a towel or bowl for a short, comfortable practice. Soften your jaw and hands. Breathe in gently; breathe out longer. Say, “Thank You, God, You are here.” Then speak a verse: “God is within her; she will not fall” (Psalm 46:5), or “When I am afraid, I put my trust in You” (Psalm 56:3). Put on worship and let your husband practice with you—he can give thanks out loud and remind you of what is true. You are teaching your whole person to return to peace.

Psalm 139 says God knits your baby together in the womb. These women are here to prepare for their natural birth. Hold this truth: God is knitting your baby together, and you were created for this sacred work. Prepare boldly, expect peace, and let that expectation become part of your atmosphere.

Why I want you to learn the evidence

Birth timelines have changed dramatically. A lot of women are given a short clock and then told their body is failing when it does not fit that clock. Modern hospital birth also lives inside systems shaped by liability, scheduling, protocols, and reimbursement - not always the full patience of physiological birth. I want you informed, not afraid. Evidence Based Birth is one of the strongest places I have found to study controversial hot topics with actual statistics and sources, not simply “because we said so.”

Evidence Based Birth resource shelf

For researched articles and statistics, explore: water breaking / PROM • VBAC • labor progress • induction • water birth.

One important example: water breaking is one part of a labor story, not a stopwatch that replaces individualized assessment. If membranes rupture, your team looks at the whole picture—gestational age, baby’s wellbeing, infection-risk factors, labor pattern, and your preferences. Learn the evidence, ask clear questions, and make decisions with informed consent rather than fear.

Module three • mind, language + soul

Guard your gates. Take every thought captive.

Birth is spirit, body, and soul. The mind can become a gate for peace or fear. The language you repeat matters: not because you can control every outcome with a sentence, but because words shape attention, expectation, choices, and the way the body reads threat.

In Hebrew thought, the heart, levav, is more than a feeling; it is the inner place of direction, thought, desire, and decision. That makes birth preparation more than positive thinking. We bring the inner life before God and ask what belief is directing us. Scripture calls us to take thoughts captive—not to deny reality, but to refuse agreement with fear.

I heard a case study that has never left me: a group of women who wanted a VBAC were studied, and the women who said they were “trying” for a VBAC ended up with c-sections. The word trying matters. It can become an agreement that says, “I may not actually do this.” I am not teaching denial; I am teaching intentional words. Say what you are believing for and prepare your mind, mouth, body, and atmosphere to agree with it.

You may also hear stories of placebo and nocebo effects—how expectations can change symptoms and physiological stress responses. I use those stories as a picture: fear-heavy birth content can make the nervous system brace. That does not mean a hard birth is someone’s fault. It means we get to be intentional about what we watch, repeat, and allow into our imagination.

I used to be scared of hemorrhage because of other women’s stories. Then I learned that they once began calling 500 mL a hemorrhage after a vaginal birth - the same general amount people donate in a standard blood donation. I began asking myself: what happens physiologically if I let my mind go there and believe I am hemorrhaging? My body would panic, brace, and stop partnering with peace. I chose to stop rehearsing someone else’s emergency. I asked Holy Spirit to show me what story I had picked up, released it, learned the facts, and kept my eyes on the God who was with me.

Your soul & nervous system: freedom prayer

Your soul is like an inner stream, and the Holy Spirit is the faithful keeper who helps clear what has become tangled or heavy. Pregnancy and birth can touch old fear, trauma, abandonment, control, past births, grief, and hidden agreements in other areas of life. Your nervous system may not know the difference between a present birth wave and an old story it learned to brace against. Sit quietly and ask: “Holy Spirit, what fear, memory, agreement, or borrowed story is taking up space in me around birth?” Name what surfaces. Bring it honestly to Jesus. Release the agreement: “I release the belief that I am unsafe, alone, powerless, or destined to repeat this story.” Ask, “Jesus, what is true?” Receive what He gives, then let your body respond with a slow breath, soft jaw, and open hands.

Do not force a memory. Let Holy Spirit set the pace. When He highlights something, name it without shame. Ask Jesus where it began, what you came to believe, and what truth He wants to give you now. Bring the person, fear, or story into forgiveness; release the agreement; receive the truth; then let your body answer with slow breathing, an unclenched jaw, and rest. This is not about digging up pain for pain’s sake. It is about clearing what is blocking peace so spirit, soul, and body can move together.

Relationship questions

Do I believe God is knitting my baby together? Do I trust Him to bring provision, instruction, dreams, and wisdom for delivery?

Body questions

Do I believe my baby and body are made to work together? What happens in me when I hear that?

Hidden-fear questions

What birth story am I still carrying? Where else in life do I brace, control, or expect danger?

Favor questions

Where have I believed I need to work hard enough to deserve peace? What would it mean to receive favor as a gift?

Watch my full birth stories on YouTube to hear how God showed up in dreams and visions, prepared me for hard moments in birth with specific instructions, provided what I needed, and even began speaking to me about future children before conception. God is willing. Are you open?

Module four • hydration, minerals + living water

Hydration is more than drinking plain water.

Pregnancy and postpartum ask your body to circulate more fluid, build blood volume, support the placenta, regulate temperature, digest food, and—if you are nursing—make milk. Hydration becomes more usable when it is paired with minerals, food, and a steady rhythm rather than a giant water number you force at the end of the day.

Start your day with minerals.

Before the rush: drink a mineral-rich cup and eat breakfast. During the day: keep a drink where you sit, pair fluids with meals, and use broth, fruit, tea, milk, raw milk, and mineral drinks alongside water. Raw milk is one of my favorite nourishing hydration options because it brings fluid, protein, fat, natural carbohydrates, and minerals together in a simple glass. Before nursing: bring your drink to the chair before you sit down. Think cellular hydration: water plus the minerals and nourishment that help your body use it.

Warm honey-lemon mineral cup

Warm water, lemon, honey, and a tiny pinch of mineral salt. Sip with eggs, oats, or another real breakfast.

Warm NORA tea

Traditional blend: nettle, oatstraw, red raspberry leaf, and alfalfa. Brew a nourishing infusion and add honey or lemon if you enjoy it.

Citrus coconut refresher

Coconut water, lime or orange, ice, mint, and a pinch of mineral salt.

Ruby berry mineral cooler

Muddled berries or a splash of juice, still or sparkling water, lemon, ice, and a tiny pinch of mineral salt.

What minerals are doing while you hydrate

During pregnancy, blood volume rises by roughly 40–50%. Your body needs fluid volume, sodium, potassium, magnesium, and the raw materials from food to build and move that expanded circulation. Minerals help fluid balance across cell membranes, nerve signaling, muscle function, and the steady work of the heart and blood vessels. That is why I do not teach “just drink more water.” I teach water plus minerals, protein, food, and a consistent rhythm.

NORA is traditionally nettle, oatstraw, red raspberry leaf, and alfalfa. Nettle and oatstraw are loved in mineral-rich infusions; raspberry leaf is traditionally used as a uterine-prep tea; alfalfa is often included as a nourishing herb. The point is not that one tea does everything. The point is a daily ritual of fluids, minerals, rest, and intentional nourishment. The warm honey-lemon cup supports an easy morning hydration rhythm. Cold coconut citrus gives fluid plus a bright, drinkable option. The ruby berry drink brings fruit and vitamin C into the ritual.

Molecular hydrogen water + my testimony

Molecular hydrogen water is water that contains dissolved hydrogen gas. Kangen machines use electrolysis and provide different water settings for home use. I love it because I genuinely drank more, used it in my tea and food, and built a real hydration rhythm around it.

When I switched my body healed of life long eczema, killaris Polaris, ovulation pain, a frozen shoulder and my milk supply became so much more luscious. I also have friends who switched who had growth restriction babies and no longer struggled.

It’s not miracle water it just helps hydrate the body the way God intended and what your body decides to repair is different for everyone so not everybody has same results.

That is my testimony, not a promise of the same result for every person. A water machine is one practical home tool; it never replaces nourishing food, rest, individualized care, or wise support.

Module five • nutrition for a growing baby

Feed the woman who is building a baby.

Nourishing Traditions-style food and the Brewer approach both bring us back to a simple truth: pregnancy is not a season for underfeeding. Your body is growing a baby, placenta, fluid, and expanded blood volume. Give it steady meals, protein, minerals, carbohydrates, satisfying fats, and enough rest to use them.

My testimony: high blood pressure led me to the Brewer diet.

With my first baby, I had high blood pressure. That became the doorway that led me to the Brewer diet. I learned that my body needed more nourishment—not restriction: real meals, protein, minerals, salt to taste, hydration, and steady food through the day. As I began feeding my body this way, my high blood pressure resolved. That experience changed how I prepared for every pregnancy after. I am sharing the exact framework that helped me because food became one of the simplest, most practical ways I could partner with what my body was building.

The Brewer diet, plainly

Dr. Tom Brewer taught a well-nourished pregnancy approach: adequate protein, real meals, salt to taste, hydration, and no food fear. A commonly shared Brewer framework aims for roughly 80–100 grams of protein a day, but use it as a nourishment lens instead of a scorecard. Eggs, meat, dairy, beans, lentils, fish, and the foods that work in your home all count. I found the Brewer approach after I had high blood pressure with my first baby. I was looking for answers and found a completely different way to see pregnancy nourishment: my body was not asking to be restricted—it was asking to be fed. I began prioritizing real meals, protein, minerals, salt to taste, hydration, and food prepared ahead. My high blood pressure resolved, and that experience changed the way I prepared for every pregnancy after. Brewer taught that pregnancy places a huge demand on the body because you are building a baby, placenta, amniotic fluid, and a major increase in blood volume. The practical approach is simple: eat enough protein throughout the day, do not skip meals, include satisfying fats and carbohydrates, salt food to taste, and make nourishment so available that it does not depend on a perfect day. It gave me a way to build blood and support pregnancy instead of fearing food.

Explore the historical Brewer Pregnancy Diet resource.

Your nourishing meal rhythm

Breakfast 1: eggs + fruit + raw milk

Eggs cooked in butter or ghee, fruit, and a glass of raw milk or mineral drink.

Breakfast 2: protein yogurt bowl

Greek yogurt or cottage cheese with berries, nut butter, cacao, mineral salt, and a spoon of honey if desired.

Lunch 1: beef + rice bowl

Ground beef, warm rice, avocado, greens, and citrus or salsa.

Lunch 2: chicken-rice soup

Chicken, broth, rice, carrots, celery, and mineral salt—make enough for tomorrow.

Dinner 1: meatballs + polenta + greens

Protein, a satisfying carbohydrate, greens, and a sauce or broth for warmth.

Dinner 2: nourishing taco bowl

Ground beef, rice, black beans, cheese, avocado, tomatoes, lime, cilantro, and mineral salt.

Why specific foods matter

Eggs: a rich food source of choline, a nutrient involved in fetal brain and nervous-system development. Fruit + vegetables: vitamin C supports collagen production and helps the body absorb iron from plant foods. Protein + fats: help make meals satisfying and steady. Broth, greens, beans, meat, dairy, seeds: practical mineral-rich choices.

Mitochondria: give your cells a good environment

Your cells need fuel, sleep, movement, daylight, and recovery. Build regular meals. Get outdoors. Let sunlight touch your skin with wisdom; sunlight is how the body makes vitamin D, a nutrient important for bone, immune, and overall health. Put bare feet on the earth if that practice helps you slow down. A pregnancy body is doing enormous work; it deserves energy, not another harsh program.

Breakfast 1: eggs + sweet potato plate

Eggs, roasted sweet potatoes, yogurt and berries, nut butter, and a warm drink.

Breakfast 2: chocolate date “Snickers”

Split Medjool dates, fill with peanut or almond butter, dip in dark chocolate, then top with chopped nuts, cacao nibs, and flaky salt. Pair with yogurt, eggs, or another protein-rich breakfast.

Lunch 1: beef + sweet potato bowl

Ground beef, sweet potato, greens, avocado, pumpkin seeds, and lemon.

Lunch 2: chicken rice mineral soup

Chicken, broth, rice, carrots, celery, greens, lemon, and salt. Freeze extra.

Dinner 1: meatballs + polenta + greens

Double the recipe and freeze individual portions for postpartum.

Dinner 2: nourishing taco bowl

Build a warm bowl with seasoned ground beef, rice, black beans, cheese, avocado, tomatoes, cilantro, lime, and mineral salt. Make extra taco meat for the freezer.

Dessert ideas that still nourish

Chocolate date “Snickers”

Split Medjool dates; remove pits; fill with peanut or almond butter; drizzle with melted dark chocolate; add peanuts and flaky salt. Keep chilled for an easy sweet bite.

Chocolate avocado pudding

Blend ripe avocado, cacao powder, milk or raw milk, a pinch of mineral salt, vanilla, and honey or maple syrup to taste. Top with raspberries, cacao nibs, and coconut.

Dates and labor

Small studies and reviews have explored date-fruit consumption in the last weeks of pregnancy. Some report a more favorable cervix at admission, less induction/augmentation in some groups, or a shorter first stage of labor. It is encouraging, not a promise. Enjoy dates as a nourishing late-pregnancy food, not a way to force labor on command.

Module six • prepare the body

Make room without forcing your body.

Birth preparation is not about getting “perfectly aligned.” It is about a body that can breathe, move, soften, rest, and respond. Avoid staying collapsed back into the couch all day when possible; change positions, walk, squat with support, and practice the forward-leaning shapes that feel good.

Birth ball hip circles

Sit tall on the ball and make slow circles or figure eights. Breathe into side ribs and back body.

Backward chair sit

Face the chair back as if sitting backward at dinner. Rest forward and let the pelvis move instead of slouching into the tailbone.

Opening hips

Hold a chair or counter; take a supported squat or shift gently side to side. Small range counts.

Open ribs

Hands around lower ribs. Breathe into the side and back ribs, then exhale longer and lower the shoulders.

Helpful resources: The Body Ready Method was a fun, helpful program for me. Spinning Babies also offers well-known education on comfort measures, fetal position, and birth preparation.

My breech-baby testimony

With my fourth birth, I was dealing with a breech baby. Someone gave me a word of knowledge about something in my heart I had not released to the Lord—my baby was trying to be my heart and protect that place. When I released it, my baby flipped. Every woman I have shared that picture with who processed with the Holy Spirit has told me the baby flipped too. This is my testimony, not a formula or a reason to blame yourself if a baby remains breech. Bring your whole story to God and use wise breech education and care alongside your prayer.

Module seven • the fourth trimester

Mother the mother: warmth, boundaries, and rebuilding.

The fourth trimester is not an afterthought. You are recovering from birth, feeding a baby, shifting hormonally, and becoming new again. Treat the first weeks as a season of warmth, food, bonding, and fiercely protected rest.

Days in bed

Make life small. Rest, feed baby, eat warm food, drink beside every feed, and let someone else do the door, laundry, and dishes.

Bond before hosting

You do not owe visitors access to your tender first days. “We are resting and bonding; please text first” is a complete sentence.

Warm dishes

Soup, stew, meatballs, eggs, rice bowls, potatoes, oatmeal, broth, cooked fruit, tea, and warm milk are easy to receive when you are tired.

Replenish gently

Ask your provider about postpartum lab work or nutrients that fit you. Food-first anchors include protein, iron-rich foods, vitamin-C foods, minerals, and fluids. Supplements to ask about for your own plan can include a prenatal/postnatal multivitamin, iron if indicated, vitamin D, magnesium, omega-3s, choline, and electrolytes.

Freezer meal plan

Breakfast freezer foods

Breakfast burritos, egg muffins, baked oatmeal squares, cooked sausage, roasted sweet potatoes.

Lunch freezer foods

Chicken-rice soup, beef-and-potato soup, broth portions, meatball bowls.

Dinner freezer foods

Meatballs in red sauce, shredded chicken, taco meat, cooked rice, roasted vegetables.

Easy snack foods

Date Snickers, yogurt bowls, cheese, boiled eggs, fruit, nut butter packets.

Grocery list, organized

Proteins: eggs, ground beef, chicken thighs, meatballs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, cheese, beans. Carbohydrates: rice, oats, potatoes, sweet potatoes, tortillas, sourdough. Produce: greens, carrots, celery, frozen berries, bananas, citrus, avocado. Mineral + pantry: broth, honey, pumpkin seeds, nut butter, tea, mineral salt, cacao, dates. Preparation: freezer bags, labels, paper bowls if cleanup needs to stay low.

Busy boxes for younger siblings

Ages 2–4

Chunky puzzle, reusable sticker book, animal figures, play dough, snack cup.

Ages 5–7

Coloring tray, magnetic tiles, lacing cards, audio story, simple snack.

Ages 8–11

Lego challenge card, watercolor set, card game, independent read-aloud basket.

Teens

Meal-reheat list, laundry reset, sibling outdoor time, grocery/helper role, prayer list.

Module eight • speak it until it feels familiar

Record these declarations in your own voice.

My practical hack: record these in Voice Memos in your own voice, then add gentle music behind them in an editing app. If you do not want to deal with it, text me and I will edit it for $25. Read one slowly every day; let your own voice train your heart to remember what is true.

Text Sylvia for declaration-audio editing

Put “Safe in My Covering” by Cageless Birds in your playlist. Let it be a reminder: you are not caged by fear, and you and your baby are safe in the covering of God.

1. Favor over my birth

“Father, I receive Your favor as a gift. I am not going into labor striving to earn a peaceful story; I am going into favor, led by Your Spirit. I release the belief that I have to perform, prove myself, control every detail, or work hard enough to deserve peace. Your grace is not payment for my preparation. It is a gift. I prepare because I am loved. I eat, rest, move, pray, learn, and make a plan because wisdom is beautiful—but I do not put my confidence in a checklist. I put my confidence in You.

You go before me into every room, every conversation, every decision, every contraction, every surprise, and every moment after my baby is born. I ask for favor over my body, my baby, my timing, my husband, my support people, the atmosphere around me, and the words spoken over me. I bless the place where I will labor. I ask that it become a worship tunnel, a private place of meeting with You. You are not distant from birth. You are near. Your Spirit is with me. Not by might, not by power, but by Your Spirit.

I choose thanksgiving. With every wave I can say, ‘Thank You, God, You are here. Thank You, my body can open. Thank You, this wave is bringing my baby closer.’ I receive favor to stay present instead of racing ahead in my mind. I receive favor to rest in the spaces between. I receive favor to hear wisdom, ask questions, and make peaceful decisions. I am not forgotten, not abandoned, and not alone. I am held by the God who gives grace freely.”

2. Peace over my body and birth hormones

“God has not given me a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind. I take every fearful thought captive and bring it under the love of Jesus. I release borrowed birth stories. I release the need to rehearse emergencies that are not mine. I release words that make my body brace. I choose words of life over my body and baby. My mind is becoming a peaceful place. My nervous system is allowed to settle. My jaw can soften. My shoulders can drop. My hands can unclench. My breath can slow. My ribs can widen. My belly can be soft. My pelvic floor can yield. I can meet one wave at a time.

I bless the hormones God designed for birth. I welcome the quiet, warmth, privacy, touch, eye contact, worship, reassurance, laughter, and loving presence that help my body feel safe. I receive the comfort of oxytocin and the strength to be fully present. I bless my husband to speak life, give thanks, protect the room, and remind me who I am when I forget. I bless every wave to do its work. I do not have to fight it. I can breathe low, make sound, move, sway, lean forward, rest, and respond to what my body is asking for.

God is within me; I will not fall. I am fearfully and wonderfully made. The One who formed my body understands it better than I do. I declare that pressure is not a prophecy of panic. I choose to stay soft and connected. I choose to receive peace that passes understanding. I choose to return to the next breath, the next thank You, the next wave, and the faithful presence of God. My birth is not a place where fear gets the final word. Peace has a place here. Worship has a place here. The Spirit of God has a place here.”

3. Life, purpose, and protection over my baby

“My baby is fearfully and wonderfully made, knit together by God in my womb. I bless every cell, organ, system, connection, and detail of this baby’s body. I speak life over the brain, heart, lungs, bones, muscles, blood, nervous system, digestion, immune system, senses, and sleep. I bless this baby with peace, strength, belonging, and a deep knowing that they are wanted. I thank You that You are present in the hidden work I cannot see. You are not careless with this life. You know this baby by name. You know the days written for them. You have purpose over their story.

I bless my womb as a peaceful home. I bless the sound of my voice, the sound of my husband’s voice, the worship in our home, and the prayers spoken over this baby. I declare that our home will carry life-giving words. I reject fear-based language, hopeless language, and the stories that try to make my heart small. I guard my gates. I choose what I watch, listen to, receive, and repeat. I give Holy Spirit permission to show me any agreement with fear that needs to leave. I release it to Jesus. I receive the truth He speaks in its place.

Father, teach me to hear You clearly. Speak in dreams, Scripture, wise counsel, quiet nudges, and the moments I least expect it. I am open to Your preparation. I am open to Your provision. I am open to Your instruction. I bless this child’s arrival with peace and welcome. I declare that no fear gets ownership of this story. This baby belongs to God, is loved by God, and is being carried in a home that is learning to trust God more deeply.”

4. Covering, provision, and postpartum peace

“Father, I receive Your covering over the days before birth, the birth itself, and the fourth trimester. I release the pressure to bounce back, carry everything, entertain everyone, or prove I am fine. I bless my body to rest, recover, nourish, and receive. I welcome warm food, broth, mineral drinks, raw milk, protein, good fats, water, support, sleep, and gentleness. I receive help without guilt. I receive boundaries without apology. I receive quiet bonding without feeling that I owe the world access to me or my baby.

I ask for provision in practical ways: food in the freezer, loving hands, peaceful visitors, wise words, financial provision, enough sleep, and the courage to ask for what I need. I bless my milk supply, my nourishment, my hydration, and my body’s return to strength. I bless the relationship between me and my baby. I bless the relationship between my husband and our baby. I bless our older children with security, inclusion, and peace. Let our home be a place where new life is received with warmth.

I declare that I am safe in Your covering. I am not caged by fear, old pain, or another person’s story. I am free to be present. I am free to rest. I am free to say yes to help and no to what drains me. You are my refuge and strength, an ever-present help. You supply what we need. You are near in the midnight feedings, the tender tears, the first days, the healing, the joy, and the learning. I receive this season as holy. I bless my body, I bless my home, and I bless the life You have entrusted to us. Amen.”

Worship for your birth space

Build a peaceful birth playlist.

Download it before labor. Keep it gentle, familiar, and peaceful enough that your husband can press play without asking you what you want. These are declaring songs: peaceful words that keep the room full of truth.

“Here Again” — Elevation Worship

Soft music with no words

Use DappyTKeys’ instrumental soaking piano music for quiet prayer, resting between waves, or newborn bonding. Put it at the beginning of a separate no-words playlist so it is ready when you need the room to soften.

Make three playlists: quiet early labor, worship through waves, and meeting baby. Let the music become a familiar signal that says: “God is here.”

Module nine • week by week

Speak specifically over your baby’s development.

Each week, read what is developing, ask God what He wants you to notice, then speak the declaration.

Keep this all in one journal.

Use one journal for your weekly development notes, the way you engage with God, dreams, prayers, questions, Scriptures, and every declaration. Write the question. Sit with Him. Record what He highlights. Then speak the week’s decree out loud. Months from now, you will be able to look back and watch the beauty of the story He created with you and your baby.

Week 4

Developing: the early foundations, implantation, and first nervous-system structures.

Engage God: “Father, what are You celebrating in this tiny beginning?”

Declare: “I bless the tiny beginning of this life. Every first cell and connection is held by God.”

Week 5

Developing: early heart, brain, spinal cord, and circulation.

Engage God: “What do You want me to bless as baby’s heart and circulation form?”

Declare: “I speak life over baby’s developing heart, brain, spine, and blood flow.”

Week 6

Developing: brain growth, facial features, and limb buds.

Engage God: “What does Your peace sound like over baby’s growing brain and spine?”

Declare: “I bless every forming feature, limb, and pathway in baby’s growing brain.”

Week 7

Developing: hands, feet, and early body systems.

Engage God: “What strength are You building in our family this week?”

Declare: “I speak blessing over every tiny hand, foot, and system.”

Week 8

Developing: major organs and systems in early formation.

Engage God: “How are You faithfully tending the hidden work inside me?”

Declare: “Father, cover every organ and system doing quiet work.”

Week 9

Developing: a new season of detail and steady growth.

Engage God: “What is one fear You want me to exchange for Your peace today?”

Declare: “I bless this transition and speak order, strength, and peace.”

Week 10

Developing: bones, joints, fingers, toes, and organs.

Engage God: “What truth do You want me to speak over baby’s forming body?”

Declare: “I speak life over every bone, joint, finger, toe, and organ.”

Week 11

Developing: lengthening, movement, and body detail.

Engage God: “How are You inviting me to slow down and notice this life?”

Declare: “I bless quiet movements and steady growth.”

Week 12

Developing: continuing maturation as first trimester closes.

Engage God: “What promise do You want me to carry into this next season?”

Declare: “Thank You for carrying us through this first season.”

Week 13

Developing: facial features, bones, and length.

Engage God: “Where are You showing me Your careful craftsmanship?”

Declare: “I speak life over every hidden detail.”

Week 14

Developing: strengthening body and facial movement.

Engage God: “What would it look like to receive Your provision this week?”

Declare: “I receive strength and rest while I bless baby’s growth.”

Week 15

Developing: bones, muscles, and growing responsiveness.

Engage God: “What do You want gratitude to sound like in my home today?”

Declare: “I bless my baby’s strength, senses, and future.”

Week 16

Developing: movements that may become noticeable.

Engage God: “How are You teaching me to trust Your pace?”

Declare: “Every flutter reminds me of life and hope.”

Week 17

Developing: fat stores, bones, and muscles.

Engage God: “What kind word do You want me to speak over this baby today?”

Declare: “I bless the steady strengthening happening inside me.”

Week 18

Developing: hearing and nervous-system maturity.

Engage God: “What part of Your character do You want to reveal to me now?”

Declare: “Let the sounds around us carry peace and belonging.”

Week 19

Developing: senses and protective skin coating.

Engage God: “How are You inviting me to welcome these first movements?”

Declare: “I speak peace over every sense and layer of protection.”

Week 20

Developing: middle-pregnancy growth and complexity.

Engage God: “What practical preparation would bring peace, not pressure?”

Declare: “Thank You for the life You are writing.”

Week 21

Developing: digestion, movement, and strength.

Engage God: “What sounds do You want surrounding my baby this week?”

Declare: “I bless baby’s growth and rhythms.”

Week 22

Developing: sleep-wake rhythms and senses.

Engage God: “What protection and peace do You want me to declare today?”

Declare: “I bless peaceful rhythms and a peaceful home.”

Week 23

Developing: lungs and senses continuing maturation.

Engage God: “What are You writing in this pregnancy that I cannot yet see?”

Declare: “I speak peace over developing lungs and awareness.”

Week 24

Developing: lungs, brain, and systems maturing.

Engage God: “How can I partner with Your care in one small way today?”

Declare: “God, cover every hidden system with Your care.”

Week 25

Developing: strength, body fat, and muscle.

Engage God: “What restful rhythm are You inviting me into?”

Declare: “I choose rest, nourishment, and peace.”

Week 26

Developing: response to sounds and familiar voices.

Engage God: “What do You want me to release from my words and thought life?”

Declare: “I choose words that carry life.”

Week 27

Developing: brain, lungs, and preparation for next growth.

Engage God: “What wisdom are You giving me for the next right step?”

Declare: “God gives me wisdom for the next right step.”

Week 28

Developing: rapid brain growth and body maturation.

Engage God: “How can I honor my body’s need for nourishment and rest?”

Declare: “I bless endurance, comfort, and provision.”

Week 29

Developing: fat stores and maturity for outside life.

Engage God: “What familiar voice do You want my baby to hear most?”

Declare: “I nourish myself and baby with grace.”

Week 30

Developing: brain, body, and reserves for birth.

Engage God: “What do You want me to bless as we enter this next trimester?”

Declare: “We are not rushed by fear.”

Week 31

Developing: practice breathing movements and strength.

Engage God: “Where are You asking me to receive support with joy?”

Declare: “I speak strength over baby and softness over my body.”

Week 32

Developing: bones, muscles, lungs, and systems.

Engage God: “What provision do You want me to thank You for today?”

Declare: “Peace, not pressure, leads my preparation.”

Week 33

Developing: brain and immune-system maturation.

Engage God: “How are You preparing both me and baby in this season?”

Declare: “God is already present in every decision ahead.”

Week 34

Developing: breathing practice and reserves.

Engage God: “What does softness look like in my body and faith today?”

Declare: “I receive grace for rest and wise preparation.”

Week 35

Developing: growth and possible settling for birth.

Engage God: “What anxious timeline can I place back in Your hands?”

Declare: “I release control and receive courage.”

Week 36

Developing: lungs, digestion, and readiness.

Engage God: “How are You already present in the decisions ahead?”

Declare: “We are held, guided, and not alone.”

Week 37

Developing: early-term growth.

Engage God: “What would wise, peaceful preparation look like this week?”

Declare: “I bless baby’s timing and continued growth.”

Week 38

Developing: final refining and growing in their timing.

Engage God: “What control are You inviting me to surrender to You?”

Declare: “I release the clock and receive peace.”

Week 39

Developing: last days of womb maturation.

Engage God: “How are You covering us as we draw nearer to birth?”

Declare: “I am going into favor, led by Your Spirit.”

Week 40

Developing: arrival close or still unfolding.

Engage God: “What is Your invitation for my heart in these final weeks?”

Declare: “God is not absent from waiting or the unexpected.”

Week 41

Season: a continued time of waiting, maturing, listening, and being present with your baby.

Engage God: “Holy Spirit, what do my baby and I need from You today?”

Declare: “I refuse the pressure of a date on a calendar. I bless my baby’s continued time in my womb and release the clock into God’s hands. I am not behind. God is present in this waiting. I receive wisdom for each decision, peace for my body, and favor over the next step. I bless this baby with strength, maturity, and a peaceful arrival.”

Week 42

Season: extra days to rest, ask questions, pray, receive support, and listen for wisdom.

Engage God: “Father, what are You inviting me to release and receive in this space?”

Declare: “I release fear, comparison, deadlines, and every story that says waiting means something is wrong with me. My due date is an estimate, not a ruler over my peace. I ask Holy Spirit for clear instruction, wise support, and grace to stay grounded in truth. I bless my body to remain soft, nourished, hydrated, and responsive. I bless my baby with continued growth and peace. I am held, I am guided, and I will take this one day at a time.”

Week 43

Season: a time to stay close to God, make informed choices, and keep blessing your body and baby.

Engage God: “Holy Spirit, show me what faith, wisdom, and love look like for us today.”

Declare: “Father, I release this entire birth story to You again. I am not abandoned in a long wait. I bless every day with provision, rest, nourishment, support, and discernment. I receive the courage to ask every question I need to ask and the peace to make each decision with You. I declare that Your goodness does not have an expiration date. My baby is loved, my body is worthy of care, and I am still going into favor. Thank You for carrying us, leading us, and staying near in every part of this story.”
